run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Social Network
Namespace: social-network

A social network with unidirectional follow relationships, implemented with loosely-coupled microservices, communicating with each other via Thrift RPCs.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The social network application in namespace social-network is up and its sampled traffic is successful, but the workload custom-service is not: Deployment custom-service (3 replicas) currently has all three pods stuck in Pending because its pod template carries an added init container 'hang-init' that runs '/bin/sh -c "sleep infinity"' and never terminates. Revision 1 of the Deployment (ReplicaSet custom-service-5c68f797, created 17:28:11Z) had no init container and its pods did start custom-service-main; ReplicaSets of revisions 2 and 3 (custom-service-5d95dbc564 and custom-service-6c4f898445, both created 17:28:18Z) both contain hang-init, and the live Deployment's kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration still shows a template with only custom-service-main. The three current pods report Initialized=False reason ContainersNotInitialized with message 'containers with incomplete status: [hang-init]', the main container is waiting in PodInitializing and has never started, and the Deployment reports unavailableReplicas=3 with kube_deployment_status_replicas_available=0 while all 27 other deployments report 1. Nodes are Ready without pressure and the pods are all Scheduled, so scheduling capacity, image pulls and container crashes are not the cause. No evidence of failure was found on the social network services themselves (sampled nginx-web-server spans are HTTP 200, compose-post-service log has only its startup line). Prometheus holds a single sample at 17:28:35Z inside the authorized window, so no baseline exists and no latency/error-rate trend can be claimed.

claims.text: Deployment custom-service in namespace social-network has spec.replicas=3 but status.unavailableReplicas=3 and updatedReplicas=3 with no readyReplicas/availableReplicas field, and its status condition is Progressing/ReplicaSetUpdated naming ReplicaSet custom-service-6c4f898445.

The pod template of Deployment custom-service contains initContainers [hang-init] with image busybox:1.36 and command ["/bin/sh","-c","sleep infinity"], beside container custom-service-main (image python:3.9-slim, command python3 -m http.server 8080).

ReplicaSet custom-service-5c68f797 (revision 1, created 17:28:11Z) has no initContainers in its pod template, while ReplicaSets custom-service-5d95dbc564 (revision 2) and custom-service-6c4f898445 (revision 3), both created 17:28:18Z, both contain the hang-init init container with '/bin/sh -c sleep infinity'.

The live Deployment custom-service carries annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration describing a pod template with only the custom-service-main container (no initContainers), so the applied manifest differs from the running template that includes hang-init.

All three current custom-service pods (custom-service-6c4f898445-cth2v, -nzsx6, -z67bf) are phase Pending with Ready=False and Initialized=False, reason ContainersNotInitialized, message 'containers with incomplete status: [hang-init]'; their init container hang-init is running (started 2026-11-21T17:28:19Z) and container custom-service-main is waiting with reason PodInitializing, so the main container never started.

Pod events in social-network show the three revision-1 pods custom-service-5c68f797-* starting container custom-service-main at 17:28:15Z and being stopped (reason Killing) at 17:28:18Z, while the revision-3 pods record 'Created container: hang-init' at 17:28:18Z and 'Started container hang-init' at 17:28:19Z with no start event for custom-service-main.

At 17:28:35Z kube_deployment_status_replicas_available for namespace social-network was 0 for deployment custom-service and 1 for each of the other 27 deployments (compose-post-service, nginx-thrift, user-service, social-graph-service, media-service, post-storage-service, text-service, unique-id-service, url-shorten-service, user-mention-service, home-timeline-service, user-timeline-service and their datastores).
At 17:30:15Z the only pods in namespace social-network not in phase Running were custom-service-6c4f898445-cth2v, custom-service-6c4f898445-nzsx6 and custom-service-6c4f898445-z67bf.
All four nodes (sregym-control-plane, sregym-worker, sregym-worker2, sregym-worker3) report Ready=True with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure all False.

The sampled nginx-web-server trace rows spanning 17:28:14-17:28:33Z carry http.status_code=200 for operations /wrk2-api/post/compose, /wrk2-api/home-timeline/read and /wrk2-api/user-timeline/read (60 of the 208 span rows in that stored result were read and all showed 200); compose-post-service's pod log contains only its startup line at 17:28:03.468Z.

Prometheus has only one sample inside the authorized window for this target: count(up) returned a single point at timestamp 1795282115 (2026-11-21T17:28:35Z) with source_start_at equal to the window end, so no earlier metrics baseline exists in the queried window.

The Service listing for namespace social-network returned 30 Service objects (nginx-thrift, media-frontend, user-service, social-graph-service, compose-post-service, the mongodb/redis/memcached datastore services, etc.) and none of them is named custom-service.

Jaeger's service list for this target contains 12 services (compose-post-service, home-timeline-service, media-service, nginx-web-server, post-storage-service, social-graph-service, text-service, unique-id-service, url-shorten-service, user-mention-service, user-service, user-timeline-service); custom-service is not among them and no traces exist for it.

The init container hang-init ('/bin/sh -c sleep infinity') added to the custom-service pod template is the injected fault: because it never exits, initialization never completes, custom-service-main never starts, and the deployment rollout cannot reach any ready replica (0 available, 3 unavailable).

The rest of the application does not show this failure: at 17:28:35Z the other 27 deployments each reported 1 available replica, the sampled nginx-web-server spans in 17:28:14-17:28:33Z returned HTTP 200, and no non-Running pod other than the three custom-service pods existed at 17:30:15Z.

Pod Pending was not caused by unschedulable nodes or resource pressure: each custom-service-6c4f898445 pod has PodScheduled=True on sregym-worker, sregym-worker2 and sregym-worker3, and all four nodes are Ready with no memory, disk or PID pressure.

Image pull failure was not the cause: events record 'Container image "busybox:1.36" already present on machine' followed by 'Created container: hang-init' and 'Started container hang-init', and the revision-1 pods successfully pulled python:3.9-slim and started custom-service-main at 17:28:15Z.

An application crash, OOMKill or CrashLoopBackOff of the custom-service main container was not the cause: custom-service-main is in state waiting/PodInitializing with restartCount 0 and empty lastState, i.e. it never started, and no OOMKilled or Evicted condition appears for these pods.

Remove the hang-init init container (or change its command so it terminates) from the custom-service Deployment pod template and let the rollout recreate the pods; no remediation was executed in this investigation.

gaps: No change-history integration is available, so which actor or object mutated the custom-service pod template at ~17:28:18Z (between ReplicaSet revision 1 and revisions 2/3) cannot be identified; only the resulting replicas and objects are visible.

Prometheus holds a single sample at 2026-11-21T17:28:35Z inside the authorized window and Jaeger traces only span 17:28:14-17:28:33Z, so there is no baseline and no pre-incident latency or error-rate trend can be assessed.

Application logs were largely unavailable: nginx-thrift-68bc7d94df-cvmnf returned zero log lines (bytes_read 0) and compose-post-service-659bfc5898-p6mtf returned only one startup line, so absence of runtime errors in most services is unchecked rather than proven.

The error-tag trace searches for nginx-web-server and compose-post-service returned no matching traces (no_data views), which shows only that the query matched nothing; error counts for other spans remain unknown.

custom-service has no Service object in the namespace listing, produces no Jaeger spans, and its main container never started, so any downstream or user-visible impact of its unavailability is unverified.
The init container hang-init writes no logs (0 lines read), so its internal behaviour beyond 'running since 17:28:19Z' is unknown.
Secret contents could not be read and were not needed; no conclusion depends on them.
next_steps: A human should diff the live custom-service Deployment against its last-applied-configuration to confirm the hang-init init container is unauthorized and remove it.
Confirm with whoever operates the fault-injection harness whether the hang-init init container was the intended injected fault, since no change record is queryable here.
After removing the init container, verify that Deployment custom-service reaches 3 ready replicas and that a new ReplicaSet's pods pass Initialized.
If custom-service is meant to receive traffic, create/verify a Service and endpoints for it and add its own health signals, since none currently exist.
